item.title: Competitions :: RE: Competitions 2027 - 30th Anniversary!
item.description:
Author: Maxim
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 1:54 am (GMT 0)

I think it is impossible to define a percentage scale that people can agree on. Some people are easily triggered by AI cover art, for example, even if the rest is created traditionally. That seems like it’s <10% to me. On the other hand, if 10% of the code was “vibed” that seems like a lot to me. And that’s still assuming I can make an accurate measure of that percentage.

By making the boundary vague I hope that means people will err on the side of caution. I’m hoping the “AI disclosure” requirement will ensure people give a clear picture of how much it was used and that can help provide some examples for us to set clearer boundaries in future.

One thing I’d like to rule out - at least for the next competition - is an AI-positive category.

item.title: Competitions :: RE: Competitions 2027 - 30th Anniversary!
item.description:
Author: Bock
Posted: Thu Oct 29, 2026 8:02 pm (GMT 0)

Quote
We reserve the right to reject entries for these criteria:
- Too much AI. ("Too much" is up to the whims of the SMS Power! elves and cannot be defined.)

We may want to clarify this a little better before the competition happens, but in the current climate the general intention is that an entry where e.g. ~10% of the work is aided by AI would likely be accepted (e.g. an additional language, selected artwork), but an entry where ~50% of the work is done by AI wouldn't. This is not a firm rule here, but sort of aim to provide a general background intent about this.

item.title: Main :: RE: Ports created by [AI]
item.description:
Author: Centrale
Posted: Thu Oct 29, 2026 7:22 pm (GMT 0)

Bock wrote
The general idea is likely not to prevent you or anyone from posting things, but to be considerate that several people are losing motivation and interest in their work and the community given the amount of stuff released, particularly the amount of half-finished stuff.


Motivation must be intrinsic, now more than ever. External validation is nice to have and helpful, but this matter of a skillful and relatively rare ability being augmented/replaced by automation has repeated over and over throughout history. The people who appreciate and (at least partially) understand the effort and skill that goes into coding still remain appreciative and should continue to be encouraging. Not to mention the personal satisfaction that comes from a job well done. That's why there are still calligraphers, drummers, etc.

item.title: Main :: RE: Ports created by [AI]
item.description:
Author: Bock
Posted: Thu Oct 29, 2026 5:16 pm (GMT 0)

haroldoop wrote
No worries, I can stop posting AI ports.


We're currently discussing things and I don't want to rush it. The general idea is likely not to prevent you or anyone from posting things, but to be considerate that several people are losing motivation and interest in their work and the community given the amount of stuff released, particularly the amount of half-finished stuff. Perhaps a good solution would be to collate stuff in topics, e.g. "AI Ports by Haroldoop".
